prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably pick one single “best” dentist, but I can help you find the best implant provider in Charlotte by giving what to look for and how to choose. A few quick questions before I help further:
- Do you mean Charlotte, NC (not another Charlotte)?
- Are you looking for an oral surgeon, a periodontist, or a general dentist who places implants?
- Do you have insurance or a budget range, and do you prefer a downtown vs. a suburban location?

If you want a quick checklist and next steps now, here they are:

What matters most
- Specialty and training: For implants, look for a board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeon or a board-certified periodontist. Both routinely place implants and manage complex cases. A prosthodontist can be ideal for the restoration (the crown/bridge) part.
- Experience and volume: How many implants do they place per year and how long they’ve been doing implants.
- Technology: In‑office CBCT (3D X‑ray), digital implant planning and guided surgery, intraoral scanning — these improve accuracy and outcomes.
- Collaborative care: Best outcomes come when the surgeon/periodontist and the restorative dentist coordinate.
- Before & after cases and patient testimonials: Ask to see cases similar to yours.
- Follow-up and warranty: Ask about follow-up schedule and any guarantees on the implant/restoration.
- Infection control and complication management: How they handle failed implants, bone grafting, sinus lifts, etc.

Questions to ask at a consult
- Are you board-certified? How many implants have you placed in the last year?
- Do you do the restorative crown/abutment or refer to a restorative dentist?
- Will you use CBCT and guided surgery for my case?
- What are all costs (implant, abutment, crown, bone graft if needed, follow-ups)?
- What’s the timeline from implant to final crown?
- What are the risks, and how do you manage complications?

Where to search for well‑reviewed providers
- AAOMS.org (Find an oral surgeon)
- AAP.org (Find a periodontist)
- ADA Find-A-Dentist
- Local reviews (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp) — but read multiple sources.
- Ask your general dentist for a referral; they often know the best local specialists.

Ballpark cost and timeline
- Single implant + abutment + crown in the U.S. commonly runs roughly $3,000–6,000 depending on complexity and materials. Bone grafts, sinus lifts or extractions add cost and time.
- Timeline: immediate to several months; healing and integration typically 3–6 months (can be shorter with certain protocols).

If you want, tell me:
- your exact neighborhood or zip code in Charlotte,
- whether you prefer a periodontist/oral surgeon,
- and whether you have insurance.

I’ll then give a short list of highly rated local specialists and clinics to consider (based on general reputation and the criteria above).
